comparisons.peer_topic: Wealth Management Non-Interest Expense Trend and Drivers
comparisons.peer_summary: Wealth Management non-interest expenses increased 5% to $20,618 million in 2024 compared to the prior year. This increase was driven by higher compensation and benefits expenses, primarily due to increased formulaic payouts to representatives on higher compensable revenues, partially offset by decreases in non-compensation expenses such as professional services, legal expenses, and FDIC special assessment costs.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and MS disclose specific drivers for changes in operating expenses or headcount within their Wealth Management segments. GS attributes a 3% headcount increase to Growth in Asset & Wealth Management, while MS attributes a 5% increase in Wealth Management non-interest expenses to higher compensation driven by formulaic payouts to representatives on higher compensable revenues. Both disclosures link personnel/resource costs directly to revenue performance in the Wealth Management division.

sentences.text: As of December 2024, headcount increased 3% compared with December 2023, primarily due to increases in Asset & Wealth Management, Risk and Compliance, partially offset by the impact of the sale of GreenSky.

Non-interest expenses of $20,618 million in 2024 increased 5% compared with the prior year, as a result of higher Compensation and benefits expenses, partially offset by lower Non-compensation expenses.
• Compensation and benefits expenses increased, primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management representatives on higher compensable revenues.
